title: Scotch whisky shipments stuck at Indian ports over a 75% vs 150% duty dispute
body: Scotch shipments are held at Indian ports because government departments disagree on the duty for bulk imports. Pernod Ricard and Diageo each have more than 40 containers awaiting clearance, and Bacardi has five. Liquor firms expect the 75% preferential rate under the India-UK trade deal, which took effect in July. The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence says bulk concentrates are unfinished goods and should pay 150%. The page says companies have refused to pay the higher rate and industry sources warn of possible supply disruptions. The page also says finance and commerce ministries are reportedly negotiating a resolution.

title: FSSAI festive crackdown seizes food worth ₹82 crore and cancels 52 licences
body: From September 1 to November 5, FSSAI inspected 56,431 food establishments ahead of the festive season. It seized nearly 3,280 tonnes of non-compliant products worth ₹81.80 crore, including paneer, ghee, milk and sweets. It cancelled 52 licences, suspended 1,133, sealed 314 establishments and issued 10,047 improvement notices. The article places the drive within tougher enforcement this year against food businesses and e-commerce companies. The page does not quote public reaction. The seized items are everyday festive staples that shoppers buy.

title: Snitch FY26: revenue up 67% to ₹834 crore, but net loss widens to ₹27 crore
body: Men's D2C fashion brand Snitch grew FY26 operating revenue to Rs 834.82 crore from Rs 498.19 crore. It raised ad and promotional spend about 30% to Rs 107.59 crore, which fell to 12.9% of revenue from 16.6%. Net loss widened to Rs 27.07 crore from Rs 1.72 crore. Operating cash flow turned negative at Rs 87.09 crore as inventory and working capital absorbed cash. The article says the brand is expanding into offline retail and quick commerce. The page does not carry public reaction. The numbers show how heavily fast-growing D2C brands spend to grow.

title: Diwali 2026 D2C sales: ₹1,328 crore GMV, with shoppers spending more per order
body: GoKwik's study estimates D2C GMV of ₹1,328 crore over the 16 days from October 21 to November 5. That is up 81% from about ₹732 crore in a 15-day comparable 2025 period, and about 70% on a like-for-like daily basis. Average order value was ₹1,389, up about 8% from ₹1,288 in September, with items per order at about 2.2. Water purifiers sold 10.6x their September level and air purifiers 4.3x, while supplements fell 14%. Of 3,274 brands analysed, 681 grew at least 50% and 42% saw lower sales. GoKwik's CEO said consumers are spending more per order without buying significantly more items.

title: Zepto Diwali: 4.68 lakh diya orders, festive hampers tripled
body: Zepto reported 4.68 lakh diya orders during Diwali. Festive hamper orders tripled versus last Diwali, festive fashion orders doubled, and flowers and garlands rose 2.5 times. Beauty had the highest demand of any category, laddu was the most-ordered sweet and Soan Papdi led by volume. Zepto credited its work with local artisans. The page says Zepto gave no absolute order volumes except for diyas, and no city-level breakdown. The numbers show people ordering festive staples on quick-commerce apps.

title: Campa Cola's festive campaign 'Tayyari Big, Tyohaar Bada Big' focuses on the preparation, not the party
body: Campa Cola's new campaign was created by McCann India and shows everyday festive work: cleaning homes, making sweets and decorating neighbourhoods. The drink appears as something shared during breaks. McCann's CCO Rahul Mathew says the aim is to carve out distinct space in a festive ad landscape where many brands use similar visuals. It runs on TV, digital and social media, and Ria Singh directed the film. The page carries no sales figures or public reaction.

title: Uber says India driver supply is lagging and fuel costs hurt; rider incentives cut, prices could rise
body: In Q3 2026 results, Uber's sales and marketing expense rose 22.4% to $1.56 billion. Management said driver supply growth lagged demand in India, and high fuel costs worsened marketplace conditions. The CFO said fuel price effects were especially visible in India and Brazil. Uber cut rider incentives versus last year and moved more toward drivers, and it acknowledged this could raise prices for consumers. Supply hours growth improved notably in India in October. This is a company explanation for fares and availability that riders have noticed.

title: Beauty brands go quick-commerce-first as Blinkit makeup searches jump 236%
body: Redseer puts beauty on quick commerce at about $1 Bn annualised GMV, growing about 90% a year. For 10 generic makeup keywords, volumes rose 236% on Blinkit and fell 76% on Amazon between Q1 2025 and Q2 2026 (1DigitalStack). Renee Cosmetics' quick-commerce share rose from about 3% to over 13% in two years, and Moxie Beauty gets over 30% of sales there. Nykaa Now expanded from 3 cities to 13 in a year, and brands are making smaller packs for quick commerce. PAC Cosmetics has stayed off quick commerce to protect its positioning.

title: ShareChat parent Mohalla Tech: FY26 revenue passes ₹1,000 crore, net loss widens 79% to ₹1,978 crore
body: Mohalla Tech's operating revenue rose 40.4% to ₹1,016.3 Cr, driven mainly by subscriptions from its QuickTV microdrama platform. Advertising revenue fell 13% as real-money gaming advertisers pulled back. The net loss grew 78.5% to ₹1,978.4 Cr, mostly from non-cash items such as share-based payments (₹739 Cr) and forex losses (₹566.9 Cr). EBITDA loss narrowed 58% to ₹91 Cr, and Q1 FY27 was EBITDA-positive at ₹9.5 Cr. The page says the company targets an FY27 EBITDA profit of ₹25 Cr.

title: GoKwik's ESOP non-compete clause puts employees' vested options at risk
body: GoKwik amended its ESOP plan, communicated in August 2026, so it can cancel unvested and vested-but-unexercised options if an employee joins one of nine named firms. The firms include Razorpay, Shiprocket, CRED and Pine Labs. The restriction runs until two years after an employee's last day. A former employee called it a shock, and current staff with large vested holdings are weighing offers against forfeiture risk. A JSA Advocates lawyer called naming competitors in an ESOP policy unusual, and another lawyer said it could be challenged. The company reportedly laid off around 120 people and did not respond to Inc42's questions.

title: IPO-bound Cult.fit faces a fresh legal challenge over the CULT trademark
body: Cofounder Deepak Poduval has petitioned the Madras High Court to cancel the CULT trademark registration held by Cultfit Healthcare, alleging forged 2017 transfer deeds. Cult.fit denies this and says Poduval signed the deeds. The Madras HC hearing on November 5 was adjourned to December 2, and a Bengaluru Commercial Court hearing is set for November 16. Poduval also filed an FIR against cofounder Rishabh Telang in August 2026, which Telang denies. Cult.fit has told SEBI its draft prospectus misdescribed trademark ownership. The proposed IPO is about ₹4,000 Cr, with a fresh issue of up to ₹950 Cr.

title: Kissht completes ₹832 crore preferential issue, with 24 new investors
body: Kissht, the listed lending platform owned by OnEMI Technology Solutions, raised ₹832.19 Cr by issuing about 2.65 Cr shares at ₹314.11 each to 34 investors. Twenty-four are new and 10 are existing shareholders. Axis Mutual Fund schemes took 63.7 Lakh shares, nearly ₹200 Cr. The raise came about four months after its IPO, which had a ₹850 Cr fresh issue. The page says the company has not disclosed how it will use the proceeds.

title: InMobi buys 30-year naming rights to Bengaluru metro station for ₹65 crore
body: InMobi will have the Ibbaluru station renamed 'InMobi Ibbaluru Metro Station' under a 30-year deal worth ₹65 Cr with Namma Metro. BMRCL says the money adds to non-fare revenue to support infrastructure. The deal comes while InMobi's IPO, first targeted for 2025, remains delayed and no draft red herring prospectus has been filed. The company has appointed four banks for the listing. It says the deal is a way to give back to Bengaluru, where it was founded 18 years ago.

title: Qualcomm layoffs: about 1,000 India jobs reportedly at risk, second round planned for January 2027
body: Qualcomm has reportedly begun a global restructuring that cuts about 3,600 jobs, roughly 7% of its 52,000 workforce. About 1,000 of the roughly 20,000 people in India could lose their jobs across Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Delhi NCR and Chennai. A second round affecting about 1,000 more India positions is reportedly planned for January 2027. One employee's Reddit post describes severance of three months' pay plus one month per year of service. The company has not confirmed the figures. The cuts are linked to a 25% drop in mobile revenue last quarter.

title: Urban festive spending set to fall 6% as inflation squeezes budgets
body: A LocalCircles survey of over 67,000 responses from 307 districts projects urban festive spending at about ₹1.97 lakh crore in 2026, down 6% from ₹2.10 lakh crore last year. 57% plan discretionary festive purchases and 31% plan none. 83% of those spending will dip into savings, and 16% will fund it entirely from savings. Apparel, footwear and accessories lead at 72%, while jewellery is down at 6%. The page describes households as 'more selective' rather than having stopped spending. Retail sales still rose 8% year on year in September, per the Retailers Association of India.

title: Smaller sweet boxes, bigger bills: inflation is changing Diwali shopping
body: Traditional sweets are about 15% pricier than last year. Pistachio prices have nearly doubled and almonds are up about 20%. Retail inflation was 5.54% in September, with food inflation at 7.74%. Onion prices are up 108.09% year on year. Households are buying smaller sweet boxes, choosing cheaper alternatives and cutting back on gifts. The page notes these are stated intentions from the LocalCircles survey, not actual purchases.

title: Dhanteras 2026: gold sales hit ₹60,000 crore as buyers go lighter and smaller
body: Gold sales were estimated at about ₹60,000 crore, up 15-20% in value, though quantity sold was roughly unchanged because high prices limit purchases. Delhi 24-carat gold was ₹1.46 lakh per 10 grams on 6 November, against ₹1.32 lakh last Dhanteras. Shoppers favoured lightweight pendants, bangles and chains, 1-5 gram coins and 18-carat pieces. Digital gold drew younger buyers, with purchases starting at ₹10 on one platform. Old-gold exchange helped many fund new purchases.

title: Gold-hit households look to informal channels, fashion jewellery and lab-grown diamonds
body: About 29% of household buyers planning to buy gold on 6 November intend to use cheaper informal channels, while 71% would buy only from jewellers who give proper bills (LocalCircles, 42,000+ respondents). The World Gold Council says July-September jewellery consumption fell 20% to 99.9 tonnes, though value rose 16%, and bar and coin demand fell 40%. Import duty was raised from 6% to 15% in May 2026. On Amazon India during the festive period, fashion jewellery purchases rose over 50%, lab-grown diamond jewellery tripled and silver idols grew about 2.7 times.

title: Festive online sales: shoppers log in but hold back on big-ticket buys
body: Redseer put the first leg of online festive sales (8-18 October) at $7-8 Bn, with nearly 100 Mn shoppers placing over 350 Mn orders. Another dataset showed online festive sales of ₹29,800-30,900 Cr, down 7-10% from ₹33,200 Cr a year earlier. Counterpoint says smartphone sales fell 16% year on year in the first three days. Its Tarun Pathak said, 'Platforms have seen strong traffic, but conversions have been weak.' LocalCircles' Sachin Taparia said, 'Household earnings are not rising, and inflation continues to rise.' The 2025 base was boosted by the September 22 GST cuts.

title: Carmakers post strong October wholesales on festive push, but Diwali fell later this year
body: SIAM data show domestic passenger vehicle wholesales of 5,28,384 units in October, up 12.4% year on year. Maruti was up 20.5%, Tata Motors PV 20.9% and Hyundai 16.7%. Kia hit its highest-ever monthly sales for the second straight month, and Toyota fell 26.7%. Diwali fell on November 8 this year versus October 20 in 2025, and FADA had recorded a record 5.57 lakh retail sales in October 2025 after the GST cut on small cars. The page quotes no buyers.

title: Counterpoint expects festive smartphone volumes to fall 12% as buyers lean on trade-ins
body: Counterpoint expects festive smartphone volumes to fall 12% while market value grows 5%, meaning people are buying fewer but pricier phones. Trade-in volumes in October and November are expected to be 50% higher than in regular months. Premium upgrade financing runs ₹60,000-1 lakh, and device-protection plans attach 30-40% more often on premium than mid-range phones. Premium users upgrade every 12-24 months. This is a forecast, not a final tally.

title: Delhi bars non-BS6 outside vehicles from November 1 as winter plan begins
body: From 1 November to 31 January, vehicles registered outside Delhi that don't meet BS6 standards are barred from entering the capital, with AI-powered ANPR cameras at the borders. Delhi-registered pre-BS6 vehicles need a valid PUC certificate or cannot buy petrol, diesel or CNG. Over 10 lakh NCR vehicles may be affected, with about 2 lakh non-BS6 vehicles in Gurugram and Faridabad alone. The page says daily commuters will be hit and penalty details were not yet out.

title: 57% in NCR rate enforcement of Delhi's old-vehicle curbs as poor
body: A LocalCircles survey of 18,243 Delhi-NCR residents found 57% rated enforcement poor or very poor and 15% rated it good. 43% said the curbs came without adequate planning, causing traffic chaos. On day one, 14,930 vehicles were checked and 1,539 turned back. Some commuters estimate cabs could add ₹500-1,000 a day, owners of BS-IV vehicles called the curbs 'unfair', and Gurugram transporters warned of 2-3 day delivery delays.

title: Calling rules in India: caller name display and spam-call changes in November
body: Operators must start showing the caller's name (CNAP) on 4G and higher networks from 1 November 2026. Rules already in force from about 18 October require operators to flag likely spam numbers using AI/ML and notify the user. Transaction-support calls need explicit consent valid for seven days. Around 17 November, automated calls must be declared to operators in advance or be treated as unsolicited commercial communication. The page is a business-compliance roundup with no public reactions.

title: Railways suspend platform tickets at six Delhi stations for Diwali-Chhath rush
body: Platform tickets are suspended from 3 to 14 November at New Delhi, Delhi Junction, Hazrat Nizamuddin, Ghaziabad, Anand Vihar Terminal and Anand Vihar Halt. Platform entry is limited to passengers with confirmed tickets, with exemptions for those accompanying elderly, sick or disabled passengers and women needing assistance. A permanent holding area outside Platform 16 at New Delhi can hold about 7,000 people and has 150 toilets each for men and women. The page carries no passenger quotes.

title: Mumbai bans rockets and aerial firecrackers till 25 November after Diwali fire spike
body: The BMC issued a prohibitory order on 9 November banning rockets and aerial firecrackers until 11:59 pm on 25 November. Violators face up to six months' jail, a fine or both. The Mumbai Fire Brigade got 142 fire calls on 8 November, 137 of them firecracker-linked, and the most were in Borivli-Kandivli at 53. Videos of residential building fires circulated on social media, and authorities urged residents to celebrate responsibly.

title: After Binance hack, 59% of Indians favour a complete crypto ban: LocalCircles
body: A LocalCircles survey of over 43,000 responses across 311 districts found 82% have little or no trust in crypto, and 66% have zero trust, up from 49% in 2021. 59% favour a complete ban. 76% say nobody in their household trades or invests in crypto, and 56% would be willing to use the RBI-backed digital rupee. The survey follows Binance's 29 October hack, which Chainalysis put at about $5.9 billion.

title: Startups are selling the meet-up: paid dinners, hobby clubs and low-pressure gatherings
body: The page shows 'Last Updated: October 22, 2026', not a separate publication date. Startups are turning dinners, hobby clubs and shared activities into paid ways for adults to meet new people. It cites Eventbrite's 2026 Social Study on growing interest in 'low-pressure gatherings' such as puzzle competitions and flower arranging, and notes those findings come from Eventbrite's own marketplace. Misfits raised ₹5 crore seed funding in May 2025. The author argues the hard part is getting strangers to pay again after the first meeting.

title: India-US trade deal still unsigned as Democrats win Congress; exporters wait for relief
body: Democrats won both chambers of the US Congress in the midterms, and the new Congress takes office on January 3, 2027. Mike Williams of The Williams Group says Democrats are puzzled that the Trump administration has not concluded a trade agreement with India: "everyone is mystified why there is no trade deal." He expects 'significant pushback' on tariff and trade policy, and a friendlier tone toward India. He cautions against expecting a full reversal, because Trump keeps substantial executive powers, so immediate tariff relief for Indian exporters is uncertain. The page gives no tariff rates. For textile, gems and engineering workers, the practical message is to keep waiting.

title: US plan to scrap H-1B 60-day grace period draws over 31,000 comments
body: The Trump administration's proposal to end the 60-day grace period for laid-off H-1B workers had 31,383 posted comments by Tuesday night, up from about 27,000 on November 2. The grace period also covers L-1, O-1 and TN workers and their dependants. Without it, workers who lose their jobs would generally have to leave the US. About 70% of the 406,348 approved H-1B petitions in USCIS's fiscal 2025 report involved beneficiaries born in India, so Indian techies are the most exposed. Two related proposals are also open: a $70,000 charge on institutions for initial Optional Practical Training (8,947 comments), and an end to deference on extension reviews (comments due November 13). The article quotes no advocates or workers.

title: Rupee recovers about 3% from May record low of 96.9650 but oil keeps it under pressure
body: The rupee hit a record low of 96.9650 per dollar in May 2026 and traded at 94.97 in early trade on 2 November. Brent crude was $114.13 on 29 October and $109.95 on 2 November. Forex reserves fell from a record $785.706 billion (week ended 4 September) to $721 billion (week ended 16 October). The RBI raised the repo rate by 0.25 point to 5.50% on 7 October. Analysts say dearer oil raises dollar demand. Kotak NEO forecasts a range of 94.40 to 95.60. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the rupee may be undervalued by many estimates. A weak rupee makes imports, foreign travel and overseas tuition costlier.

title: Petrol and diesel prices hold steady across metros despite volatile crude
body: Pump prices were 'stable' on 10 November. Delhi petrol is Rs. 102.12 a litre and diesel Rs. 95.20. Mumbai is Rs. 111.21 and Rs. 97.83, and Hyderabad is Rs. 115.69 and Rs. 103.82. Bengaluru is Rs. 110.82 and Rs. 98.78. The article says India depends heavily on crude imports, so crude prices, taxes and rupee-dollar depreciation influence fuel rates. Commuters and transporters have so far been spared a pump-price hike even as crude has stayed above $100 for much of the month. The article carries no public reaction.

title: Commercial LPG up again before Diwali while domestic cylinder stays frozen
body: From 1 November, the 19 kg commercial LPG cylinder rose by Rs 10 to Rs 17 in the metros, the third straight monthly hike by the article's count. Delhi went from Rs 2,810 to Rs 2,820, Kolkata from Rs 2,954 to Rs 2,971, Mumbai from Rs 2,764.50 to Rs 2,775 and Chennai from Rs 2,983 to Rs 2,994.50. The 14.2 kg domestic cylinder is unchanged for a sixth month at Rs 942 in Delhi. It was last raised by Rs 29 on June 7. The article says crude rose 11-12% in October, with Brent above $113. It calls the hike 'a spoilsport in Diwali'. Dhabas, canteens and small eateries feel the commercial rise first.

title: Indian airlines extend Saudi flight cancellations; Umrah pilgrims and Gulf workers affected
body: Akasa Air has suspended Jeddah flights through November 18 and Riyadh through November 30. Air India and Air India Express have suspended Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam through November 14. IndiGo has cancelled Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah through November 14, citing ongoing airspace restrictions. Passengers can get a full refund or free rebooking. The Indian consulate in Jeddah is running 24x7 control rooms. It says Saudi carriers still fly from Jeddah and Madinah to India, and flynas added extra flights to Lucknow, Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kozhikode and Kochi. The page was last updated November 1. Pilgrims and workers are being told to confirm bookings with airlines before travelling.

title: Fuel rates unchanged on Chhoti Diwali: Delhi petrol Rs 102.12, CNG Rs 86.98/kg
body: On Chhoti Diwali there was no change in fuel prices anywhere in India. Delhi petrol is Rs 102.12 a litre and diesel Rs 95.20. Kolkata petrol is Rs 113.51, Patna Rs 113.37 and Hyderabad Rs 116.15. Delhi CNG is Rs 86.98 a kg, and Hyderabad's Rs 112.00 is the highest listed. The article says international crude has fluctuated amid Middle East tensions while Indian prices have held. Families driving home for the festival avoided a pump-price shock. It also explains the SMS route (RSP plus dealer code to 92249 92249) for checking local rates.

title: Gold at Rs 1,48,800 per 10 g and silver at Rs 1,94,500 a kg on Dhanteras eve
body: Ahead of Dhanteras (Friday), gold rose Rs 2,200 to Rs 1,48,800 per 10 g in Delhi, from Rs 1,46,600, and silver rose Rs 1,500 to Rs 1,94,500 a kg, per the All India Sarafa Association via PTI. Last year's Dhanteras price was Rs 1,32,400 for gold and Rs 1.7 lakh for silver. Global spot gold rose nearly 2% to USD 4,125.25 an ounce. Traders said buying 'gathered pace' ahead of the festival. Monarch PMS's Dhruv Joglekar noted gold is up about 13% since last year. The page also links the move to hopes that the US may seek an early resolution to the Iran conflict.

title: AIIMS Delhi 'live population' billboard goes viral, shows India at about 1.48 billion
body: A video of the AIIMS Delhi billboard claims India's population crossed 1,48,16,37,145 on November 10 at 7:27 pm. A user named Yash asked Grok to check it. Grok said the figure of about 1.4816 billion matches UN-based projections but that the board is a 'demographic projection clock', not a real-time birth and death tracker. Worldometer put mid-2026 population at 1,476,625,576, and projections suggest India could cross 1.5 billion by 2028. Many users questioned where the data comes from.

title: Ramayana breaks BookMyShow record with 1.40 lakh tickets in an hour
body: Ramayana reportedly sold over 1,40,000 tickets in one hour on BookMyShow, the highest hourly figure for an Indian film on the platform. It beat Dhurandhar 2 (1,09,170) and Pushpa 2 (1,07,650). The film opened on November 5, and the surge came in the extended Diwali holiday. Trade reports cite about 91,500 bookings between 9 and 10 am on Monday against 54,760 in the same hour on Sunday. The article stresses these are peak hourly numbers, not total sales. The film's X account posted, 'Breaking records, one hour at a time.'

title: Ramayana crosses Rs 823.50 crore worldwide by Day 6 as 'best Monday in Indian cinema history' is claimed
body: Citing Sacnilk, Business Today reports a worldwide total of ₹823.50 crore, with ₹440.45 crore nett in India and ₹297 crore overseas. Day 6 India nett was ₹94.10 crore, 12.5 per cent lower than Monday's ₹107.50 crore, which the article calls the 'best Monday in Indian cinema history'. It credits festive holidays, discounted weekday tickets and 'positive word of mouth'. In North America it took $1.37 million on its first Monday, a record for an Indian film there. Part Two is scheduled for Diwali 2028. Trade figures vary between outlets and the numbers are early.

title: Chhath rush: Northern Railway sets up holding areas at Delhi stations for people heading east
body: Northern Railway has arranged for passengers travelling to eastern India for Chhath. A permanent holding area exists at New Delhi, and a second one was commissioned at Anand Vihar Terminal this year, alongside a temporary one. They have UTS counters, toilets, ticket vending machines, catering stalls and 'May I Help You' booths. Officials are monitoring crowds at major Delhi-area stations, and unscheduled special trains will be added as needed, according to CPRO Himanshu Shekhar Upadhyay. No passenger counts are given. For migrant workers going home to Bihar and UP, this is the annual scramble for a seat.

title: Delhi High Court protects Amitabh Bachchan's name, image and voice from misuse
body: The Delhi High Court granted a permanent injunction restraining 'the unauthorised commercial use of his name, image, voice and other aspects of his identity'. Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav passed the order on November 5. The misuse covered apps, WhatsApp messages, quiz books, posters and domain names. One defendant built an app called 'Amitabh Bachchan Video Call'. Another sent WhatsApp messages using his photo to promote a purported 'Kaun Banega Crorepati' lottery. Four defendants settled, and the order extends to unidentified infringers. The court noted that unauthorised use could falsely suggest he endorses a product. The topic is relevant to ordinary Indians because of the fake-lottery messages.

title: 'Only GPay': Karan Johar's school sports day story shows how GPay became the word for UPI
body: On Koffee with Karan season 9, Karan Johar told Kareena Kapoor Khan and Saif Ali Khan about a school sports day. The snack counter took only Google Pay, Kareena had no cash, and another parent paid for them. Her line, as Johar recalled, was 'Only GPay'. The article uses it to show how 'GPay kar do' is said for any UPI payment, whichever app people use. It frames this as a brand name becoming generic for a service. It gives no financial figures.

title: Bhuvneshwar Kumar's T20I comeback ends in fan calls to retire
body: Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 36, returned to India's T20I side after four years out. His New Zealand series ended badly in the fifth T20I at Hamilton, where Tim Seifert hit two sixes in his sixth over, which cost 20 runs. He was dropped for the fourth T20I in Auckland, which India lost by 87 runs. The article's table lists 0/49, 1/50, 0/40 and 0/41 across the games he played, though its own text gives inconsistent figures for the last match. Fans on X were harsh, with one saying 'one wicket' after '19 overs 170 runs', and another joking he 'made a comeback and retired in a single series'. The article itself says retirement calls after one series are premature and that selectors should review his role.

title: Hardik Pandya set to leave Mumbai Indians for Punjab Kings in swap for Arshdeep Singh
body: Mumbai Indians and Punjab Kings have agreed a trade that sends Hardik Pandya to Punjab and Arshdeep Singh to Mumbai. It still needs BCCI ratification. Hardik returned to Mumbai before the 2024 season and replaced Rohit Sharma as captain. Mumbai then missed the playoffs twice in three seasons. An IPL source said 'Hardik is happy to play under Shreyas Iyer', who is expected to stay Punjab's captain. The article says Punjab's owners found it difficult to give up Arshdeep after his long association with the franchise. It also flags Hardik's fitness after several injury setbacks. Fan reaction is not reported on the page.

title: India beat New Zealand by four runs via DLS in rain-hit Wellington ODI
body: India won the second ODI in Wellington by four runs under DLS and took a 2-0 lead in the five-match series. New Zealand made 134, and Gurnoor Brar took 4-30 with a double strike that left them 53-5. India were 113-7 off 26 overs when rain stopped play, four runs ahead of the DLS par score of 109. Shubman Gill was out for a golden duck and Virat Kohli for seven, both to Jacob Duffy. Shreyas Iyer's 30 was the top score in the chase. Auqib Nabi took his first two international wickets. The article carries no player quotes, but the close finish and the top-order failures are the talking points.

title: ISL 2026-27 opening week draws 65 million YouTube views
body: The ISL season opened on 10 October under a new club-led model, and the first five matches drew 65 million YouTube views and 52 million viewers. Bengaluru FC v Sporting Club Delhi had 8.9 million views. Inter Kashi v Kerala Blasters peaked at 349,073 concurrent viewers on the English feed. The league channel added 120,000 subscribers to reach 2.7 million, with 1.6 million live chat messages and reactions. The page gives no fan quotes, so the 1.6 million live interactions are the only sign of how fans responded.

title: IPL stars reportedly want Rs 40 crore retention deals
body: Citing a Cricbuzz report, Business Today says at least two high-profile IPL players have told their teams they 'would consider staying only if their financial demands are met'. The reported demand is up to Rs 40 crore, and in one case it is linked to captaincy. For comparison, Rishabh Pant's 2025 contract with Lucknow was Rs 27 crore and Shreyas Iyer's was Rs 26.75 crore. A Rs 40 crore retention would take about 26.7% of an expected Rs 150 crore purse, a figure that is not formally confirmed. The article has no direct statements from players or franchises. It says the demands could force teams to rethink budgets and push other players to ask for more.

title: India win silver and bronze at ISSF World Championship in Doha
body: Niveditha Veloor Nair won individual bronze in the women's 25m standard pistol with 567-13x. She, Manvi Jain and Simranpreet Kaur Brar then took team silver with 1,682-33x. Jain finished eighth and Brar 10th in the individual event. India's tally at the Doha championships stands at seven medals: one gold, five silver and one bronze. The report is a straight results piece with no fan or public reaction.

title: Ramayana first-day X reviews: Yash praised, Ranbir Kapoor criticised
body: Viewers on X were divided on Ramayana on release day, 5 November. Yash's Ravana was the most-cited highlight, and the Jatayu v Ravana face-off was called thrilling. One IMAX viewer said it left them speechless. Others found Ranbir Kapoor's Rama dull, and one user wrote 'Massive budget, zero soul' and gave it 1.5/5. Slow pace, weak music, long runtime and a Sita fight sequence that is not in the original epic drew complaints. A viral post mockingly called it a '4000 Crore movie', which the article does not verify. Several posts called it 'average', and one suggested waiting for OTT.

title: Ramayana Part 1 breaks BookMyShow hourly record on first Monday
body: Ramayana: Part 1 sold more than 1.20 lakh tickets in one hour on BookMyShow on Monday, beating Jawan's earlier benchmark of 86,000. The 9-10 AM hour alone saw about 91,500 tickets, up 67% from 54,760 in the same hour on Sunday. The surge was tied to the extended Diwali holiday. The article says advance sales were over Rs 100 crore before the 5 November release. It also says Sacnilk reported the film crossing Rs 500 crore worldwide by Day 5. The page quotes no viewers. The record bookings sit alongside the split social-media verdict on the film.

title: Ramayana tickets hit Rs 2,600 in Ahmedabad IMAX recliners
body: On BookMyShow listings checked on 6 November, the top price for Ramayana was Rs 2,600 for IMAX 3D recliners at PVR Palladium Mall, Ahmedabad. Other IMAX 3D seats there were Rs 1,600 to Rs 1,900, and classic seats at Rs 1,600 were nearly fully booked. Surat's Rajhans Precia IMAX was Rs 1,450 to Rs 1,500. Regular 2D shows started around Rs 500. The film runs 3 hours 15 minutes, and the two-part budget is put at around Rs 4,000 crore. The piece reports no viewer comments on prices. It says most premium categories sold out in the festive rush, which shows many people paid the premium.

title: AR Rahman's Ramayana song 'Mangal Rang' draws qawwali debate
body: 'Mangal Rang' from Ramayana, composed by AR Rahman, was released around 25 October. Arijit Singh and Shreya Ghoshal sing it, and Kumar Vishwas wrote the lyrics. It celebrates Rama and Sita's wedding. Listeners on X called it 'qawwali-coded' and compared it to Rahman's 'Kun Faya Kun'. One user wanted classical instruments and Sanskrit lyrics and said the spiritual element was missing. Rahman told Hindustan Times that artists must keep evolving. Singer Armaan Malik said how listeners interpret music is subjective.

title: Jailer 2 opens with Rs 59.70 crore India net
body: Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 opened with Rs 125.25 crore worldwide gross and Rs 59.70 crore India net from 16,599 shows, per Sacnilk data cited in the piece. Tamil contributed Rs 43.35 crore, Telugu Rs 12.50 crore and Hindi Rs 3.50 crore. That compares with Jailer (2023) at Rs 48.35 crore India net, and Coolie (2025) at Rs 65 crore India net and Rs 151.10 crore worldwide. The article says disputes over digital release windows involving multiplex chains including PVR INOX reportedly hit the Hindi release in north India. The page has no audience quotes and calls the opening 'spectacular'.

title: Suriya's Scene crosses Rs 100 crore India net in six days of Diwali run
body: Suriya's action comedy Scene reached Rs 100.70 crore India net and Rs 117.04 crore gross by Day 6. Day six alone added Rs 3.30 crore net from 2,865 shows, with Tamil at Rs 2.51 crore and Telugu at Rs 79 lakh. The Week calls it a 'stellar Diwali-week run'. A Sacnilk preview had projected Rs 28 crore for its first three days in its 'expected' scenario. The page carries no audience reaction, so the numbers are the only signal of how it was received.

title: Jailer 2 heads to Prime Video on 12 November amid cut-role complaints
body: Prime Video India announced Jailer 2 will stream from 12 November in Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada and Hindi. The theatrical release was on 15 October, with Rs 8.21 billion at the box office as of 4 November per Sacnilk, and a 175-minute runtime. Indian media reports of 30 extra minutes online are not confirmed in the article. Viewers had criticised the theatrical cut for trimming Mohanlal, Vijay Sethupathi and Hrithik Roshan, and some said scenes teased in the trailer were missing. Producer Antony Perumbavoor said the change was not happy news for Malayalis. Actor Mirnaa Menon said she was sure director Nelson had strong reasons.

title: Bigg Boss 20 viewership reportedly falls as fans complain about Qazi Touqeer's screen time
body: Deccan Chronicle reports that Bigg Boss 20's weekly viewership has dropped from 30 million to 7 million. It names no source for the figures, so treat them as unverified. Fans say popular contestant Qazi Touqeer has had much less airtime in recent episodes and see it as the likely reason for the decline. Qazi has a large following outside the house, and several celebrities, including Rohit Shetty, have voiced support. The show airs on Colors and JioHotstar and is hosted by Salman Khan.

title: Qualcomm layoffs begin in India: more than 1,000 employees likely impacted
body: Qualcomm has started layoffs in India. The headline says more than 1,000 employees are likely affected, while the body cites ground reports of about 1,000. Qualcomm has not confirmed a number. Unofficial reports put severance at three months of salary plus one month for each year of service. The article says handset revenue fell 25 per cent last quarter. The page quotes no employees directly. It relies on Reddit posts and one person claiming to be a laid-off Qualcomm employee.

title: Qualcomm begins layoffs in India: what is the severance package being offered?
body: Qualcomm has about 20,000 employees in India. Industry estimates put possible cuts at 600 to 1,200 roles, roughly 3 to 6 percent of that workforce, and Qualcomm has not confirmed this. CEO Cristiano Amon's October 19 memo announced a 'performance-focused reduction' with notifications starting in November. Anonymous Reddit users say they have received notices. One self-described former employee lists two months' notice pay, one month's pay per year of service, RSUs, one year of insurance, leave encashment and a December bonus. That user says the placement help through Randstad is mostly nominal, so laid-off staff must find new jobs themselves. None of this is verified by Qualcomm.

title: IT hiring takes divergent turns in Q2 as workforce numbers shift
body: September-quarter filings show the big four IT firms moving in different directions. Infosys added 4,480 to reach 3,32,542 and TCS rose by 4,258 to 5,98,056. HCLTech added 6,450 to reach 2,30,339 and hired 6,136 freshers, against 1,056 in the prior three months. Wipro fell by 6,716 to 2,36,328, about 2.8%. Attrition was 12.7% at Infosys (voluntary), 13.3% at TCS, 12.8% at HCLTech and 13.8% at Wipro (voluntary). The article cautions that firms define attrition differently and that headcount drops do not necessarily mean people left voluntarily.

title: 'Relocate or leave': IBM tells workers as it halts US green card sponsorship
body: IBM is ending US green card sponsorship, and the report says workers were told to relocate or leave. The US Department of Labor suspended PERM applications for eight companies: Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini. USCIS data shows 1,611 H-1B visas approved in 2026, down from 2,045 in 2025. IBM Consulting employs about 1,50,000 people out of a worldwide workforce of about 2,90,000. An IBM spokesperson told Reuters that participation in the visa programmes 'has been declining over the years.' The article carries no reactions from affected workers.

title: India's hiring surge: AI and ML roles jump 32% in Naukri JobSpeak October
body: Naukri JobSpeak for October shows white-collar hiring up 14% year-on-year and AI/ML roles up 32%, with the index at 2,836. General software and QA hiring is up only 1%. Global capability centres are up 18%. By city: Hyderabad 15%, Pune 14%, Delhi-NCR 13%, Bengaluru 12%. Info Edge CEO Hitesh Oberoi said 'Some of October's growth reflects last year's festive-season base.' The piece presents AI/ML demand as driven by mid-to-senior roles and tells freshers to look at data operations, QA automation and platform support.

title: Microsoft employee's 'day in my life' reel takes a dig at layoffs, crosses 2 million views
body: A reel by Sid (@sidincorporate) spoofs the polished 'day in my life at Microsoft' vlog format and jokes about layoffs. It has crossed 2 million views on Instagram. Commenters wrote 'Brother chose to roast A Day in My Life at Microsoft' and called it an 'updated version of a day at Microsoft.' Another praised him for having 'cracked the layoff trap.' Many comments point to the uncertainty and pressure employees feel as companies restructure.

title: Gujarat trader's Diwali bonus: over ₹1 lakh cash on a silver plate for each employee
body: Surat textile trader Ramswaroop Munde gave each of his 20 employees over ₹1 lakh in cash on a silver plate for Diwali. The notes ranged from ₹10 to ₹500. He told Aaj Tak the gesture came from growing up in poverty and understanding the financial strain on families at festival time. He called his staff 'an extension of his family.' Employees were stunned and at least one woman cried on camera. The video went viral and many users praised his generosity.

title: Diwali 2026: Jodhpur company Mediagarh gifts four cars to employees
body: Mediagarh, an education marketing agency with over 100 staff, gave four cars at its Dhanteras event on November 6: a Tata Harrier, a Hyundai i20 and two Tata Tiagos. The company has followed a pattern of one car in year one, two in year two and four in 2026. It also gave 15 silver and 15 gold performance awards. Founder Pankaj Budhwani called it 'an expression of gratitude towards employees.' The article says festive-season sales rose up to 20% in value, while smartphone, smart TV and laptop unit sales fell up to 15%.

title: Delhi firm gifts iPhone 16 to staff for Diwali, internet asks 'Any vacancies?'
body: Rohini-based Financersaab left iPhone 16 handsets on employees' desks for Diwali instead of the usual sweets. A 15-second Instagram video of the surprise went viral. The company has not said how many staff got phones or what they cost. Reactions mixed praise with envy. Some joked 'Any vacancies?' and one user said their own office had not even given a box of sweets. Some viewers doubted the clip or suggested it looked AI-generated, which the company denies.

title: Shrinking reach, silent bans: inside Instagram's surge in content restrictions
body: SFLC.in data cited by Newslaundry shows 268 content restrictions and 83 account restrictions in October across Meta platforms, X, Reddit and YouTube. Instagram had 174 posts and 59 accounts restricted, the highest of these platforms. Creator Raghav Trivedi (772,000 followers) said his reach reportedly fell from 100 million to 30 million in October and that he has had 'eight videos taken down.' Amit Kilhor thinks keywords may trigger bulk removals. Meta's standard response was that removals were done on legal request. Creators complain that no explanation is given for a removal or restoration.

title: Instagram's 2026 AI labelling rules: what brands, influencers and creators in India need to know
body: This law-firm commentary says Instagram renamed its 'AI creator' badge to 'AI-generated profile' on 31 August 2026, after first testing the label in May 2026. The IT Rules amendment took effect on 20 February 2026 and cuts the takedown window to three hours from 36. The author says creators and brands ask whether the label is mere housekeeping or carries legal risk. He warns that 'honest creators may be penalised for volunteering while others escape notice.' Instagram has not said how much reach is lost under the policy. The piece quotes no creators directly.

title: Instagram's AI thinks you're a teen. How do you prove it wrong?
body: On 9 November 2026 Meta announced a worldwide expansion of its AI age checks. The article asks what an Indian user wrongly flagged as under 18 can do. It notes that Teen Accounts began in India in February 2025. It also notes that the DPDP Act treats anyone under 18 as a child, with child-data provisions scheduled to start in May 2027. Meta's announcement gives no error rate. The article quotes no users, so reaction is not covered.

title: Rohit Shetty warns fans about fake accounts after viral post on Gaurav Gupta's Bigg Boss 20 roast
body: A Facebook post carrying Rohit Shetty's name criticised mocking humour after comedian Gaurav Gupta roasted ScoutOP and Love Gill on a Diwali-special Weekend Ka Vaar. Many assumed Shetty wrote it. He clarified on Instagram that he has no official presence on Facebook or X and that Instagram is his only account. He called accounts claiming to be him on other platforms 'fake and unauthorised.' One X user had praised him for standing up for ScoutOP, a reaction based on the fake post.
